solution: The integrand is a proper rational function. By the form of partial fraction [Table 7.2 (i)], write \(\frac{1}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \frac{A}{x+1} + \frac{B}{x+2}\). This gives \(1 = A(x+2) + B(x+1)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x\) and the constant term, \(A+B=0\) and \(2A+B=1\), so \(A=1\) and \(B=-1\). Thus \(\frac{1}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \frac{1}{x+1} - \frac{1}{x+2}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \int \frac{dx}{x+1} - \int \frac{dx}{x+2} = \log|x+1| - \log|x+2| + C = \log\left|\frac{x+1}{x+2}\right| + C\).

Here the integrand \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6}\) is not a proper rational function, so we divide \(x^2+1\) by \(x^2-5x+6\) and find that \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 + \frac{5x-5}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 + \frac{5x-5}{(x-2)(x-3)}\). Let \(\frac{5x-5}{(x-2)(x-3)} = \frac{A}{x-2} + \frac{B}{x-3}\), so that \(5x-5 = A(x-3) + B(x-2)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x\) and constant terms, \(A+B=5\) and \(3A+2B=5\), giving \(A=-5\) and \(B=10\). Thus \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 - \frac{5}{x-2} + \frac{10}{x-3}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6}\,dx = \int dx - 5\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,dx + 10\int \frac{dx}{x-3} = x - 5\log|x-2| + 10\log|x-3| + C\).

The integrand is of the type as given in Table 7.2 (4). Write \(\frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)} = \frac{A}{x+1} + \frac{B}{(x+1)^2} + \frac{C}{x+3}\), so that \(3x-2 = A(x+1)(x+3) + B(x+3) + C(x+1)^2 = A(x^2+4x+3) + B(x+3) + C(x^2+2x+1)\). Comparing the coefficient of \(x^2\), \(x\) and the constant term on both sides, \(A+C=0\), \(4A+B+2C=3\) and \(3A+3B+C=-2\). Solving these, \(A=\frac{11}{4}\), \(B=\frac{-5}{2}\) and \(C=\frac{-11}{4}\). Thus the integrand is \(\frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)} = \frac{11}{4(x+1)} - \frac{5}{2(x+1)^2} - \frac{11}{4(x+3)}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)}\,dx = \frac{11}{4}\int \frac{dx}{x+1} - \frac{5}{2}\int \frac{dx}{(x+1)^2} - \frac{11}{4}\int \frac{dx}{x+3} = \frac{11}{4}\log|x+1| + \frac{5}{2(x+1)} - \frac{11}{4}\log|x+3| + C = \frac{11}{4}\log\left|\frac{x+1}{x+3}\right| + \frac{5}{2(x+1)} + C\).

Consider \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)}\) and put \(x^2=y\). Then \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = \frac{y}{(y+1)(y+4)}\). Write \(\frac{y}{(y+1)(y+4)} = \frac{A}{y+1} + \frac{B}{y+4}\), so that \(y = A(y+4) + B(y+1)\). Comparing coefficients of \(y\) and constant terms, \(A+B=1\) and \(4A+B=0\), which give \(A=-\frac{1}{3}\) and \(B=\frac{4}{3}\). Thus \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = -\frac{1}{3(x^2+1)} + \frac{4}{3(x^2+4)}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2\,dx}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = -\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dx}{x^2+1} + \frac{4}{3}\int \frac{dx}{x^2+4} = -\frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}x + \frac{4}{3}\times\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + C = -\frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}x + \frac{2}{3}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + C\). Here the substitution was made only for the partial fraction part and not for the integration part.

Let \(y=\sin\phi\). Then \(dy=\cos\phi\,d\phi\). Therefore \(\int \frac{(3\sin\phi-2)\cos\phi}{5-\cos^2\phi-4\sin\phi}\,d\phi = \int \frac{(3y-2)\,dy}{5-(1-y^2)-4y} = \int \frac{3y-2}{y^2-4y+4}\,dy = \int \frac{3y-2}{(y-2)^2}\,dy = I\) (say). Now write \(\frac{3y-2}{(y-2)^2} = \frac{A}{y-2} + \frac{B}{(y-2)^2}\) [by Table 7.2 (2)], so that \(3y-2 = A(y-2) + B\). Comparing the coefficients of \(y\) and constant term, \(A=3\) and \(B-2A=-2\), which give \(A=3\) and \(B=4\). Therefore \(I = \int \left[\frac{3}{y-2} + \frac{4}{(y-2)^2}\right]dy = 3\int \frac{dy}{y-2} + 4\int \frac{dy}{(y-2)^2} = 3\log|y-2| + 4\left(-\frac{1}{y-2}\right) + C = 3\log|\sin\phi-2| + \frac{4}{2-\sin\phi} + C = 3\log(2-\sin\phi) + \frac{4}{2-\sin\phi} + C\) (since \(2-\sin\phi\) is always positive).

The integrand is a proper rational function. Decompose it into partial fractions [Table 7.2 (5)]. Write \(\frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)} = \frac{A}{x+2} + \frac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}\). Therefore \(x^2+x+1 = A(x^2+1) + (Bx+C)(x+2)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x^2\), \(x\) and the constant term of both sides, \(A+B=1\), \(2B+C=1\) and \(A+2C=1\). Solving these, \(A=\frac{3}{5}\), \(B=\frac{2}{5}\) and \(C=\frac{1}{5}\). Thus the integrand is \(\frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)} = \frac{3}{5(x+2)} + \frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{2x+1}{x^2+1}\right)\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)}\,dx = \frac{3}{5}\int \frac{dx}{x+2} + \frac{1}{5}\int \frac{2x}{x^2+1}\,dx + \frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{x^2+1}\,dx = \frac{3}{5}\log|x+2| + \frac{1}{5}\log|x^2+1| + \frac{1}{5}\tan^{-1}x + C\).
